items.prompt: Black to move. With best play the position is a draw, but only one move holds it. Find it.

claims.statement: The side to move can hold the draw.
f1=Q keeps the draw.
Kd1 gives up the draw: result loss.
Kd2 gives up the draw: result loss.
Ke2 gives up the draw: result loss.
Kf1 gives up the draw: result loss.
f1=B gives up the draw: result loss.
f1=N gives up the draw: result loss.
f1=R gives up the draw: result loss.

hints: Check which of your pieces is in check or can be taken, and what the enemy king would have if you gave up a piece.
Look for a move after which the enemy has no legal move but is not in check.
Test the sacrifices: after the capture, count the legal moves the pawn's king has.
items.explain: f1=Q is the only move that holds the draw: the tablebase shows that every other legal move loses, for example f1=B, f1=N, f1=R.

hints: You have a pawn on the seventh rank and the enemy king is far away. Which squares make a stalemate possible?
Keep your king next to the pawn and near the corner, and look for moves that offer the queen only a stalemating capture.
Before pushing the pawn, ask whether the queen can take it with check; if so, consider waiting with the king and look for the stalemate net.
items.explain: The tablebase confirms the position is a draw with best play, so the defender can hold it.
